checks: Read ce4a362fe44872e9 §6. The proof applies to every real r>0. The Taylor integral from 1 to x on either side gives the stated positive weight and multiplicative factor (r+2)/r.

The weight ratios on the overlapping interiors increase strictly in t for x1<x2. On the right the new support is farther right, and on the left the removed part is farther left. Both changes have the correct sign in the two-density cross-product integral.

Integrating the cross-product against 1/t−1/u on t<u gives the first minus the second mean. It is strictly positive on a positive-area subset of the common interior, so monotonicity is strict on each side.

The quadratic Taylor coefficient at 1 gives the continuous value (r+2)/r, while the leading linear terms at infinity give (r+1)/r. Strict decrease on both sides and continuity imply strict decrease across 1.
